title: SLO Deviation Restoration Blueprint and Customer Notice Templates
author: Asha Patel
summary: Runbook and communication templates for responding to SLO deviations (latency, error-rate, throughput) that impact customer-facing services. Includes detection queries, step-by-step mitigation, escalation matrix, synthetic remediation recipes, and ready-to-send status page / customer email templates.
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical SLO deviation restoration blueprint for Redwood Inference. It covers detection, immediate mitigation, escalation, customer communications, and post-incident follow-up for service-level-objective (SLO) violations that cause customer impact. It is intended for on-call engineers, SRE leads, and customer-facing teams.

Scope
- Services covered: api-gateway, inference-router, model-worker, kv-cache
- SLOs in scope: latency (p95 / p99), availability/error-rate, embedding-failure-rate, provisioning latency for Dedicated pools
- Out-of-scope: billing pipeline, internal analytics jobs (separate runbooks)

Key SLOs and thresholds
- api-gateway: p95 latency < 200ms, error-rate < 0.1% (30d target)
- inference-router (hosted): p95 latency < 250ms, p99 < 600ms, request-error-rate < 0.5%
- model-worker: CPU/GPU queue time median < 10ms, tail queue time < 200ms
- kv-cache: hit-rate >= 85%, miss-rate < 15%

Detection signals and monitoring queries (examples)
- Prometheus (PromQL) examples:
  - api-gateway p95 latency:
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (le))
  - api-gateway error rate (5m):
    sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",code=~"5..|429"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m]))
  - inference-router queue depth per zone:
    sum(kafka_consumer_lag{topic=~"router-requests-.*"}) by (zone)
- Synthetic checks (examples)
  - Healthcheck curl to production endpoint:
    curl -s -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/health
  - Small inference synthetic: POST /v1/generate with small prompt and 64-token limit (response time < 300ms)

Initial response procedure (first 10 minutes)
1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and mark incident channel (#incident-<service>-<YYYYMMDD>)
2. Gather signal summary (metrics, traces, recent deploys, infra events) and paste to channel:
   - p95/p99 deltas, error rates, top 3 services by errors, latest deploy git SHA, recent autoscaler events
3. Run quick-sanity synthetics (curl + small inference) from two regions (us-west1, eu-west1) and paste results
4. If impact confirmed, escalate to on-call SRE + owning service lead (see Escalation matrix)
5. Decide on customer-visible status page entry within 15 minutes if: ongoing error-rate > 1% or latency > p95 * 2 for > 10 minutes

Escalation matrix (quick reference)
- Primary on-call (1st) — owns triage and initial mitigations
- Secondary on-call (2nd) — take over ownership if primary cannot resolve within 20m or needs rotation
- SRE Lead (pager) — required if incident is Sev2/Sev1 or will likely exceed 30m to resolution
- Product / Customer Success — loop in when customers are impacted for > 30 minutes or contracts are affected
- Executive Notification — follow exec-notify SOP for incidents > 4 hours or cross-region outage

Table: contact roles and criteria
Role | Pager | Escalation condition
Primary on-call | oncall-api | Any alert firing for service
Secondary on-call | oncall-api-secondary | Primary requests escalation or rotation
SRE Lead | sre-pager | Sev1/Sev2 or >30m to mitigation
Product / CS | cs-oncall | Customer-visible incident >30m
Executive Ops | exec-pager | Multi-region outage or >4h impact

Mitigation patterns (pick based on root cause signals)
- Traffic-routing fallback:
  - If a region shows high p99s, route traffic to nearest healthy region via traffic-policy: rtrctl set-weight api-gateway --region us-west1=0.0 eu-west1=100
- Cache flush / warm-up:
  - If kv-cache hit-rate drops <50% and backend is healthy, consider TTL transient bump: etcdctl put /config/kv_cache/ttl 300
- Autoscaler override:
  - For Dedicated pools: override min_replicas to provision more workers: kubectl patch hpa model-worker -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10}}' --namespace production
- Rollback deploy:
  - If a recent deploy is correlated: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway --to-revision=<previous-revision>
- Circuit breaker (soft-fail to degraded code path):
  - Flip runtime flag to degraded path: curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/api/flags -d '{"api_gateway_degraded":true}'

Customer and status page communication templates
- Status page short update (for incidents with observable customer effect):
  - Title: API: Increased latency for text-generation (partial)
  - Body (first 15m): We are investigating elevated latency affecting text-generation requests in the us-west1 region. Our engineers have identified increased queueing on model-worker GPUs and are running diagnostics. We will post updates every 30 minutes.
  - Impact: Partial regional degradation for hosted API customers. Some requests may time out or experience delays.
  - Next update: <time+30m> (UTC)
- Status page update (post mitigation):
  - Title: Incident resolved: API latency restored
  - Body: The issue impacting text-generation latency has been resolved. Root cause: a regression in model-worker queueing under burst traffic introduced by a recent scheduler change (git sha: abc1234). Mitigation: autoscaler override and rollback of scheduler change. Customers may experience transient delays while caches warm.
- Customer email template (for impacted customers; send via CS):
  - Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API latency — Update
  - Body: Hello <Customer>,

We want to notify you of a service incident earlier today that may have affected requests to the Redwood hosted API in the us-west1 region. Our team detected elevated latency and increased timeouts from ~<start-time> to ~<end-time>. We have restored normal service as of <resolved-time>.

Root cause: Regression in scheduler logic that caused worker queueing.
Impact: Partial request delays and timeouts for a subset of requests.
Action taken: Rolled back the change, manually increased autoscaler min replicas, and warmed the kv-cache.
Next steps: We will follow up with a post-incident report including mitigation details and action items within 72 hours. If you saw errors in production logs that require debugging help, please reply to this message or open a support ticket.

Sincerely,
Redwood Support Team

Runbook snippets (copyable commands)
- Check top error sources (jq filter example):
  kubectl logs -n production deployment/api-gateway --since=10m | jq -r '. | select(.level=="error") | .message' | head -n 50
- Force autoscaler min replica (k8s):
  kubectl patch hpa model-worker -n production -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10}}'
- Quick synthetic from us-west1 (bash):
  REGION=us-west1; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' https://$REGION.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}'

Game day scenarios and exercises
- Purpose: validate runbook clarity, on-call handoffs, and customer comm cadence under time pressure. Exercises are run quarterly.
- Example scenario A (SLO spike, rolling deploy correlation):
  - Inject: a canary deploy to api-gateway that increases p99 latency in eu-west1 to >1s
  - Objectives: detect synthetic failures, escalate appropriately, validate rollback, and publish status page update within 15 minutes
  - Success criteria: rollback completed within 30 minutes, status updates posted every 30 minutes, postmortem drafted within 72 hours
- Example scenario B (multi-region cache miss storm):
  - Inject: synthetic traffic that causes global kv-cache misses and elevated origin load
  - Objectives: validate cache warm-up playbook, TTL bump procedure, and traffic-policy weight change
  - Success criteria: kv-cache hit-rate back to >=85% within 45 minutes and no customer-facing errors after mitigation

On-call succession and handoff checklist
1. Primary on-call documents what was done: metrics, CLI commands, and timestamps in incident channel
2. Secondary on-call repeats checks and confirms mitigations are stable for 10 minutes
3. Handoff message template:
  - "Handoff to @<secondary> — current status: mitigation applied (rollback + autoscaler override). p95=210ms; error-rate=0.18%. Next actions: monitor caches, prepare postmortem."
4. If unresolved, escalate to SRE lead using escalation matrix

Post-incident requirements and timeline
- Within 24 hours: draft incident timeline in Confluence (primary on-call)
- Within 72 hours: full postmortem with root cause analysis, action items with owners and deadlines, and regression tests for the cause
- Within 7 days: retro with Product/CS and update runbook with any missing steps

Postmortem template (key sections)
- Summary (1-2 sentences)
- Impact (who, what, duration)
- Timeline (ordered events with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (causal chain + why safeguards failed)
- Mitigations applied (what fixed it)
- Action items (owner + due date)
- Follow-up verification (how and when we will confirm)

Runbook governance and continuous improvement
- Owners: Service owners must review and sign off runbook changes quarterly
- Game days: SRE organizes quarterly game days and publishes results and identified gaps
- Runbook edits: Changes must include a short summary and reviewer and be published in the runbook index (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+Index)

Related pages
- Service-level objectives index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Index
- Incident commander playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Commander

Appendix: quick-check checklist (copy to incident channel)
1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty
2. Post initial signal summary (metrics + deploy SHA)
3. Run synthetic from 2 regions (curl examples above)
4. Determine whether to post status page (criteria above)
5. Apply mitigation pattern (routing/rollback/autoscaler)
6. Escalate per matrix if not resolved in 20 minutes
7. Draft timeline and assign postmortem within 24 hours

End of document
